inputs.text: They’re presenting Mary Ngechi Ngethe as the convenient end of the story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, and the money supposedly recovered from her. That doesn’t answer who shaped the wider procurement process or who else may have benefited. A single committee chair taking the blame—and a claim that the money was “recovered”—could be exactly what makes the public stop asking questions. The tidy ending deserves more suspicion, not less.
